items.title: Duffy Jackson interviewed by Monk Rowe, New York City, New York, October 17, 1995
items.q: why Michael Jackson and not Duffy Jackson is successful

ctx.x: It’s all downhill from here, so—

You know it’s amazing, my dad and I, as far as I’m concerned, I don’t know maybe you can enlighten me to this, but I consider us to be the only father and son bass and drum team in the whole history of jazz. Now there might be certain people I’m not aware of. But as far as people that have come up and tried to keep the American art form alive, you know my dad played in Woody Herman’s band without a bass amp, and you heard every note. Now that means he pulled those strings. So there was the human element of…
Yeah. Music that you could kind of half listen to.
